newsitem.title: UK: Wide expectations for IPE Sept gas oil deliveries.
newsitem.headline: Wide expectations for IPE Sept gas oil deliveries.

text.p: Expectations for physical deliveries against the IPE September gas oil contract, which expires at midday on Thursday, vary greatly due to steep backwardation in the futures market, historically high prices and industry's wariness of the coming winter, traders said.
The introduction of European Union low sulphur diesel regulations on October 1 also clouded market predictions.
Estimates ranged from about 1,000 contracts to as high as 5,000, from the current estimated open interest of 10,658 contracts as of Monday. Each contract is 100 metric tonnes.
"I would say about the same as last month at 100,000-150,000 tonnes and it could even be under 100,000," said one trader. "I don't think the refiners have that much to deliver."
Deliveries against the August contract were 1,169 contracts.
"I think it will be quite a large delivery," said another trader. "I think people with material are happy to get rid of it on the screen and people are willing to grab it up."
He estimated 4,000-5,000 contracts would be open at the expiry on Thursday.
"I think we're hearing there may be some large deliveries and that is holding up the market," an oil broker said. "I think it will be more than last month's."
Speculation that one trading house was going to take a large amount of September gas oil helped boost prices over the week, traders said.
At 1515 GMT, Sept gas oil stood down 25 cents at $217.00 a tonne with a backwardation to the October contract at $6.50.
Sept gas oil rose to a contract high on Monday of $221.75, also the strongest level for the spot contract in five years.
Traders said underlying sentiment was bullish with end-user demand expected to kick in over the next month as the backwardation and steep prices have discouraged stock building.
That may also affect the number of deliveries, they said.
IPE said the record number of deliveries was 8,536 contracts in January and in September 1995 there were 1,061 contracts for delivery.
Contracts that went to delivery since January were 5,668 (February), 6,215 (March), 802 (April), 126 (May), 895 (June), and 1,216 (July).
